name: Meme Stock Squeeze
description: A massive short squeeze ignited by social media frenzy forces hedge funds into catastrophic losses as retail traders coordinate a historic buying campaign

phases.name: Social Media Frenzy
headlines: {company} stock goes viral: retail traders identify massive short interest
Social media forums explode with {company} buy calls as short interest tops 140%
Retail brokerages report record sign-ups as {company} momentum builds
phases.summary: Online communities discover extreme short interest in {company} stock. Viral posts attract millions of retail traders who begin buying shares and call options en masse, driving rapid price appreciation.

phases.name: Short Squeeze Ignition
headlines: Hedge funds scramble to cover {company} shorts as losses mount into billions
{company} options chain explodes — gamma squeeze compounds buying pressure
Multiple prime brokers issue margin calls on {company} short positions
phases.summary: Short sellers face catastrophic losses as {company} stock price doubles, then triples. Forced covering by hedge funds creates a feedback loop of buying pressure. Options market makers must delta-hedge, adding fuel to the squeeze.

phases.name: Full Squeeze — Forced Covering
headlines: {company} reaches stratospheric levels as remaining shorts capitulate
Hedge fund liquidation drives {company} to 5x pre-squeeze price
Historic short squeeze: {company} becomes most traded stock globally
phases.summary: The squeeze reaches maximum intensity. Remaining short sellers are forced to cover at any price, driving {company} to levels disconnected from any fundamental value. Trading volumes shatter all records.

phases.name: Momentum Fizzle
headlines: {company} rally stalls as buying pressure fades and volume dries up
Retail interest wanes: {company} social media mentions drop 60%
Short sellers hold firm on {company} positions as momentum collapses
phases.summary: The buying wave loses steam. Retail traders move on to the next opportunity, volume collapses, and short sellers who held their positions begin to see relief. The stock drifts back toward more normal levels.

phases.name: Pump and Dump Trap
headlines: Insiders and early buyers dump {company} shares as retail piles in
Investigations reveal coordinated {company} pump scheme — retail left holding bags
{company} collapses as sell orders overwhelm — billions in retail losses
phases.summary: It becomes clear that insiders and early coordinated buyers are selling into retail demand. When the selling wave hits, there is no support. {company} stock crashes violently, trapping late buyers with devastating losses.

phases.name: Post-Squeeze Normalization
headlines: {company} begins long descent from squeeze highs as volatility fades
Regulators announce review of short-selling rules following {company} episode
{company} settles into new trading range — squeeze veterans take profits
phases.summary: The historic squeeze is over. {company} gradually returns to more rational pricing. Regulators announce investigations and potential rule changes. The event leaves lasting scars on short-selling hedge funds.

phases.name: Fizzle Aftermath
headlines: {company} meme trade fades into memory as fundamentals reassert
Retail traders lick wounds after {company} disappointment
Short sellers profit as {company} returns to pre-hype levels
phases.summary: {company} returns to pre-hype fundamentals. The failed squeeze becomes a cautionary tale. Short sellers who held their positions are vindicated while retail traders who bought the hype take losses.

phases.name: Trap Fallout
headlines: Class action lawsuits filed over {company} manipulation — SEC opens probe
Congressional hearings announced on {company} trading manipulation
{company} retail investors organize legal action as losses crystallize
phases.summary: The aftermath of the pump-and-dump is severe. Lawsuits pile up, regulators investigate, and retail traders who were caught in the trap face significant losses. The incident damages trust in market fairness.

name: Lehman Moment
description: A systemically important financial institution collapses, threatening to trigger a cascade of failures across the entire banking system and global economy

phases.name: Institution in Crisis
headlines: Major financial institution reveals catastrophic losses on toxic asset portfolio
Shares of systemically important bank plunge 40% as balance sheet holes emerge
Credit default swaps on major bank surge to record levels — default fears mount
phases.summary: A systemically important financial institution shocks markets by revealing massive losses. The bank's stock collapses and its bonds trade at distressed levels. Questions emerge about counterparty exposure across the financial system.

phases.name: Contagion Panic
headlines: Interbank lending freezes as institutions refuse to lend to each other
LIBOR-OIS spread explodes — money markets seize up globally
Multiple banks face margin calls; counterparty risk fears paralyze trading
phases.summary: Trust evaporates from the financial system. Banks refuse to lend to each other, money market funds break the buck, and the TED spread reaches crisis levels. The entire financial plumbing of the economy is at risk of collapse.

phases.name: Emergency Bailout
headlines: Government announces emergency rescue package for financial system
Central bank opens unlimited lending facilities — 'whatever it takes' pledge
Treasury guarantees money market funds; emergency bank recapitalization begins
phases.summary: The government and central bank intervene with an unprecedented rescue package. Emergency lending facilities, bank recapitalizations, and deposit guarantees aim to restore confidence and prevent systemic collapse.

phases.name: Cascade Failures
headlines: Second major bank collapses — government rescue efforts prove insufficient
Credit markets in freefall as cascade of institutional failures accelerates
Insurance giant reveals trillions in toxic derivatives exposure — bankruptcy imminent
phases.summary: The contagion cannot be contained. Multiple institutions fail in rapid succession. Credit markets seize completely, and the real economy begins to feel the impact as lending to businesses and consumers stops entirely.

phases.name: Bailout Recovery
headlines: Markets rally as bailout details reassure investors — worst appears over
Interbank lending resumes cautiously as government guarantees take effect
Financial stocks rebound 20% from crisis lows on stabilization hopes
phases.summary: The bailout begins to work. Interbank lending slowly resumes, credit spreads narrow from extremes, and equity markets stage a relief rally. However, the recovery is fragile and a new regulatory framework is coming.

phases.name: Deep Recession
headlines: Economy enters deepest recession since the Great Depression — markets down 40% from peak
Unemployment surges past 10% as credit crunch devastates real economy
Analysts warn recovery could take years as financial system restructuring begins
phases.summary: The financial collapse translates into a devastating economic recession. Markets fall 40% from their peak. Unemployment skyrockets, housing prices collapse, and the economy enters a prolonged period of deleveraging and pain.

phases.name: New Regulatory Era
headlines: Landmark financial reform bill passes — strictest regulations since the Depression
Banks forced to raise capital buffers; proprietary trading banned
Markets stabilize under new framework — investor confidence slowly returns
phases.summary: Sweeping financial reforms reshape the banking industry. New capital requirements, stress tests, and trading restrictions aim to prevent a repeat crisis. Markets begin to price in a new, more regulated financial landscape.

phases.name: Prolonged Bear Market
headlines: Markets continue grinding lower as economic data deteriorates further
Bear market enters second year — no recovery in sight for financial sector
Government forced into massive fiscal stimulus as monetary policy hits zero bound
phases.summary: The bear market drags on. Economic data continues to worsen, corporate earnings collapse, and despite government intervention, the recovery remains elusive. Markets eventually bottom but the damage is profound and lasting.

name: Flash Crash 2.0
description: A catastrophic algorithmic trading malfunction causes markets to plunge 8% in minutes, triggering circuit breakers and raising questions about market structure integrity

phases.name: Algorithmic Meltdown
headlines: Markets plunge 8% in minutes as algorithmic trading systems malfunction
Unprecedented flash crash wipes trillions in market value in under 10 minutes
Trading systems overwhelmed — multiple exchanges report order processing failures
phases.summary: A cascading failure in algorithmic trading systems triggers an immediate 8% market crash. The speed and severity overwhelm market infrastructure. Billions of trades execute at absurd prices before anyone can react.

phases.name: Circuit Breakers Engage
headlines: Market-wide circuit breakers halt trading for the first time in years
Exchanges suspend trading as regulators assess flash crash damage
Global markets follow into freefall before emergency halts activated
phases.summary: Circuit breakers trigger across all major exchanges. Trading halts give regulators time to assess the damage. Thousands of trades executed at erroneous prices await review. The question is whether this was a one-time glitch or a systemic problem.

phases.name: V-Shaped Recovery
headlines: Markets reopen and rally sharply — flash crash deemed a technical glitch
Buyers rush in as erroneous trades cancelled; market recovers 6% from lows
Regulators confirm isolated algorithm failure — no systemic risk identified
phases.summary: Markets reopen and immediately rally. Regulators confirm the crash was caused by a single faulty algorithm. Erroneous trades are cancelled, and confident buyers step in to buy the dip. Most losses are recovered within days.

phases.name: Liquidity Crisis
headlines: Market makers withdraw from markets citing unacceptable risk — liquidity evaporates
Trading reopens to immediate selling as confidence in market structure shattered
High-frequency firms pull out en masse — bid-ask spreads widen to unprecedented levels
phases.summary: The flash crash reveals deep structural problems. Market makers and HFT firms withdraw, citing broken market structure. When trading resumes, there is almost no liquidity. Prices fall further as sellers find no bids.

phases.name: Quick Normalization
headlines: Markets fully recover from flash crash — regulators announce algorithm safeguards
New circuit breaker rules implemented within days of flash crash
Flash crash becomes footnote as markets resume normal trading patterns
phases.summary: The V-shaped recovery holds. New safeguards are quickly implemented, trading patterns normalize, and the flash crash is treated as a one-time event rather than a structural crisis. Markets move on.

phases.name: Regulatory Emergency
headlines: SEC declares market structure emergency — algorithmic trading faces temporary ban
Week of chaos continues as manual trading proves unable to handle volume
Investor class actions filed against exchanges and HFT firms
phases.summary: Regulators declare an emergency and temporarily ban certain algorithmic trading strategies. The transition to reduced-automation markets is chaotic. Prices remain depressed as structural uncertainty keeps institutional money on the sidelines.

phases.name: Market Structure Reform
headlines: Landmark market structure reform passed — algorithmic trading permanently restricted
New minimum resting times and order-to-trade ratios reshape electronic markets
Markets stabilize under new rules but permanently lower liquidity levels persist
phases.summary: Comprehensive market structure reforms are enacted. Algorithmic trading faces permanent new restrictions. Markets stabilize but operate with structurally lower liquidity, wider spreads, and reduced efficiency compared to before.

name: Pandemic Shock
description: A global health emergency triggers the fastest bear market in history as lockdowns shut down the world economy and uncertainty reaches unprecedented levels

phases.name: Health Emergency Declaration
headlines: WHO declares global health emergency — travel and hospitality stocks crater
Pandemic fears grip markets as new pathogen spreads across multiple continents
Airlines and cruise lines collapse 30%+ as international travel grinds to halt
phases.summary: The World Health Organization declares a global health emergency. Travel, hospitality, and entertainment stocks suffer immediate catastrophic losses. The market begins pricing in the possibility of widespread economic disruption.

phases.name: Lockdown Selloff
headlines: Major economies announce full lockdowns — markets suffer worst week since 2008
Broad market in freefall as economic shutdown becomes reality
VIX hits all-time high as panic selling overwhelms all asset classes
phases.summary: Governments worldwide implement lockdowns. The economic shutdown is faster and more severe than anyone anticipated. Every sector sells off — there is no hiding place. Circuit breakers trigger repeatedly as the VIX reaches historic highs.

phases.name: V-Recovery — Stimulus Surge
headlines: Unprecedented fiscal stimulus: government announces multi-trillion dollar rescue
Central bank cuts rates to zero, launches unlimited QE — markets surge
Tech stocks lead dramatic recovery as digital economy thrives in lockdown
phases.summary: Governments and central banks launch the largest coordinated stimulus in history. Zero interest rates and massive QE flood markets with liquidity. Tech and healthcare stocks surge as winners of the new digital economy.

phases.name: L-Shape — Prolonged Depression
headlines: Stimulus measures fail to stem economic collapse — unemployment hits 20%
Wave of corporate bankruptcies as lockdown extends indefinitely
Consumer spending collapses — recovery nowhere in sight
phases.summary: Stimulus measures prove insufficient against the scale of economic destruction. Businesses fail in waves, unemployment reaches Depression-era levels, and consumer confidence collapses. The market finds no floor.

phases.name: W-Shape — False Dawn
headlines: Markets rally on reopening optimism — but outbreak data tells a different story
Premature reopening sparks second wave fears; gains evaporate
Whiplash in markets: recovery hopes dashed as case counts surge again
phases.summary: An initial recovery rally fizzles as premature reopening triggers a second wave. Markets give back all gains and then some. The double-dip shakes confidence in any near-term recovery scenario.

phases.name: New Bull Market
headlines: Markets hit all-time highs despite ongoing pandemic — liquidity trumps fundamentals
Treatment breakthroughs accelerate reopening; cyclical stocks surge
The everything rally: stimulus-driven bull market defies economic reality
phases.summary: Massive liquidity injection creates a new bull market even as the real economy struggles. Treatment breakthroughs and vaccine hopes accelerate the recovery. A new market regime emerges characterized by low rates and high valuations.

phases.name: Structural Damage
headlines: Economic scarring: permanent job losses mount as industries restructure
Real estate crisis emerges as commercial property values collapse 40%
Government debt levels raise long-term sustainability concerns
phases.summary: The prolonged depression causes permanent structural damage to the economy. Entire industries are wiped out, commercial real estate faces a crisis, and government debt levels raise questions about long-term fiscal sustainability.

phases.name: Second Wave Reality
headlines: Second lockdown announced — markets crash again as W-shape confirmed
Healthcare system overwhelmed; emergency measures reimposed globally
Investors brace for prolonged uncertainty as double-dip recession takes hold
phases.summary: The second wave forces renewed lockdowns. The economic double-dip becomes reality. Markets crash again, though the decline is less severe as investors are now experienced with pandemic trading. The eventual recovery will be slower and harder.

phases.name: Post-Pandemic New Normal
headlines: Markets enter post-pandemic era — new winners and losers emerge
Remote work revolution permanently reshapes commercial real estate and tech valuations
Post-pandemic economy stabilizes but looks fundamentally different
phases.summary: Regardless of which path the crisis took, a new normal emerges. Some industries are permanently transformed while others slowly recover. The pandemic leaves lasting changes on how markets price risk and how economies function.

name: ETF Liquidity Crisis
description: A passive investing doom loop unfolds as mass ETF redemptions create self-reinforcing selling pressure that threatens to destroy the entire index investing ecosystem

phases.name: Redemption Wave
headlines: Major bond ETF breaks NAV by 5% — retail investors panic as 'safe' fund misprices
Record $80B in ETF redemptions in single day as passive investors stampede for exits
Largest ETF providers halt creations as authorized participants overwhelmed
phases.summary: A major bond ETF breaks its net asset value by an alarming margin, triggering panic among retail investors who believed passive funds were inherently safe. Redemption requests flood in at record pace, overwhelming the system.

phases.name: Liquidity Vacuum
headlines: Authorized participants can't keep up — ETF bid-ask spreads explode to 3%
Index funds forced to fire-sell underlying stocks to meet redemptions
Market makers pull bids on hundreds of ETFs — 'there is no liquidity left'
phases.summary: Authorized participants cannot process the volume of redemptions. ETF bid-ask spreads explode as market makers withdraw. Index funds are forced into fire sales of underlying stocks, creating cascading selling pressure across the entire market.

phases.name: Market Maker Rescue
headlines: Major banks step in with emergency liquidity — ETF spreads begin to narrow
Wall Street consortium commits $200B to stabilize ETF market structure
Fed signals willingness to backstop bond ETFs — 'orderly markets are essential'
phases.summary: A consortium of major banks steps in to provide emergency liquidity. With implicit Fed support, authorized participants resume normal operations and ETF spreads begin narrowing. The crisis is contained through coordinated private sector action.

phases.name: Passive Doom Loop
headlines: Index selling forces underlying stock sales which forces more index selling — doom loop confirmed
S&P 500 components crash uniformly regardless of fundamentals — passive selling indiscriminate
Active managers watch helplessly as good companies dragged down by index outflows
phases.summary: The self-reinforcing doom loop takes hold. ETF redemptions force selling of underlying stocks, which drives index values lower, triggering more redemptions. Good and bad companies crash identically as passive selling is entirely indiscriminate.

phases.name: Flash Crash Cascade
headlines: Algorithmic cascade triggers simultaneous halt on 200+ ETFs — circuit breakers overwhelmed
Multiple asset classes crash in unison as ETF arbitrage mechanisms completely break down
Markets halted after 12% intraday plunge — worst single-day decline since 1987
phases.summary: Algorithmic trading systems react to the ETF dysfunction by selling everything simultaneously. Over 200 ETFs are halted as circuit breakers trigger across all exchanges. The arbitrage mechanisms that hold ETFs together completely break down.

phases.name: Structural Reform
headlines: SEC mandates new ETF liquidity rules — minimum cash buffers required for all funds
ETF industry accepts stricter oversight in exchange for continued Fed backstop
Markets stabilize under new framework — passive investing enters regulated era
phases.summary: The SEC enacts sweeping new rules requiring ETFs to maintain minimum liquidity buffers and stress-test redemption scenarios. The industry accepts tighter regulation as the price of continued operation. Markets stabilize under the new framework.

phases.name: Active Renaissance
headlines: Passive investing permanently diminished — active managers see record inflows
Stock pickers vindicated as fundamental analysis makes dramatic comeback
ETF assets under management drop 40% as investors flee passive strategies
phases.summary: The doom loop permanently damages trust in passive investing. Active fund managers see record inflows as investors seek strategies that can discriminate between good and bad companies. The 20-year passive revolution goes into reverse.

phases.name: Market Reset
headlines: Fed forced into direct ETF purchases — 'extraordinary measures for extraordinary times'
Massive central bank intervention halts crash but trust in passive investing shattered
Markets stabilize 30% below pre-crisis levels — the ETF era may be over
phases.summary: The Fed is forced into unprecedented direct purchases of ETF shares to halt the cascade. Markets stabilize but at levels 30% below pre-crisis values. Trust in the passive investing ecosystem is fundamentally broken.

phases.name: Post-Crisis Reckoning
headlines: New market structure emerges — ETFs survive but with fundamental design changes
Passive investing share drops from 50% to 30% of market — new equilibrium found
Regulators and industry agree on redesigned ETF framework — lessons learned from crisis
phases.summary: Regardless of which path the crisis took, a new market structure emerges. ETFs survive in redesigned form with new safeguards, but passive investing's share of the market permanently declines. The crisis reshapes how markets allocate capital.

name: Quant Meltdown
description: A catastrophic factor crowding unwind as over 100 quantitative hedge funds discover they all own the same positions and attempt to sell simultaneously

phases.name: Factor Unwind
headlines: Momentum factor crashes 8% in single day — worst quant drawdown in two decades
Quant hedge funds hemorrhage capital as crowded trades reverse violently
Systematic strategy losses hit $150B as factor models fail across the board
phases.summary: The momentum factor suffers its worst single-day crash in decades as overcrowded quant positions begin unwinding simultaneously. Factor models that worked for years suddenly produce catastrophic losses across dozens of funds.

phases.name: Crowded Trade Collapse
headlines: Correlated deleveraging across 100+ quant funds creates unprecedented selling pressure
Prime brokers report record margin calls — quant funds forced to liquidate at any price
Market impact costs explode as everyone tries to exit the same positions simultaneously
phases.summary: Over 100 quantitative funds discover they all built the same positions using similar models. Correlated deleveraging creates massive selling pressure. Prime brokers issue margin calls that force further liquidation in a vicious feedback loop.

phases.name: Orderly Deleverage
headlines: Major quant funds raise emergency cash from investors — orderly unwind begins
Prime brokers coordinate exposure reduction — avoid forced liquidation spiral
Goldman and JPMorgan lead coordinated effort to prevent quant contagion
phases.summary: The largest quant funds raise emergency capital and prime brokers coordinate a managed reduction in exposure. By avoiding forced liquidation, the industry prevents the worst-case scenario of a complete systemic meltdown.

phases.name: Margin Spiral
headlines: Prime brokers force liquidation of $500B in quant positions — selling begets selling
Stocks with high quant ownership crash 30%+ regardless of fundamentals
Mid-size quant funds shutting down daily as losses exceed fund viability thresholds
phases.summary: Prime brokers lose patience and force liquidation of massive quant positions. Stocks with high quantitative fund ownership crash violently regardless of their fundamentals. Multiple mid-size quant funds announce permanent closure.

phases.name: Systemic Risk
headlines: Clearing houses face margin shortfalls as quant fund failures cascade through system
Counterparty fear grips Wall Street — banks refuse to face quant fund exposure
Fed convenes emergency meeting as quant meltdown threatens financial system stability
phases.summary: The meltdown escalates beyond hedge funds into systemic territory. Clearing houses face margin shortfalls, banks refuse to trade with quant-exposed counterparties, and the Fed convenes an emergency meeting as financial system stability comes into question.

phases.name: Industry Restructuring
headlines: Quant industry consolidates — survivors emerge stronger with better risk management
Factor investing adapts with new decorrelation requirements and position limits
Markets normalize as quant deleveraging completes — bargain hunters step in
phases.summary: The quant industry undergoes painful but orderly restructuring. Surviving funds implement better risk management and regulators introduce decorrelation requirements. Markets normalize as the excess leverage is worked off.

phases.name: Quant Winter
headlines: Investors flee quantitative strategies — $2T in quant AUM halved in months
Fundamental investors see record inflows as 'quant is dead' narrative takes hold
Factor investing faces existential crisis — academic models questioned
phases.summary: Investors lose faith in quantitative strategies entirely. Assets under management in quant funds are cut in half. A 'quant winter' descends on the industry as the academic models underpinning factor investing face fundamental questioning.

phases.name: Fed Intervention
headlines: Fed establishes emergency facility to backstop clearing house shortfalls
Government-coordinated wind-down of failed quant funds prevents systemic collapse
Financial system stabilizes but only after unprecedented central bank action
phases.summary: The Fed is forced to establish emergency facilities to backstop clearing house shortfalls. A government-coordinated wind-down of failed funds prevents full systemic collapse, but the intervention raises serious questions about market structure.

phases.name: New Quant Paradigm
headlines: Regulators mandate decorrelation requirements and position limits for systematic funds
New era of quant investing emerges — smaller, more diversified, better risk-managed
Markets enter post-quant-crisis equilibrium with permanently lower systematic leverage
phases.summary: New regulatory mandates require decorrelation testing and position limits for all systematic funds. A new paradigm of quantitative investing emerges — smaller, more diversified, and far more carefully risk-managed than the pre-crisis era.
